title: Spengler wins from pole to give BMW its first DTM victory since the comeback
dek: Bruno Spengler converted pole into victory at the Lausitzring, holding off Gary Paffett's Mercedes by 1.019 seconds for BMW's first win of its DTM return.

chapters.title: One week on from Hockenheim
text: The DTM was back on track just seven days after the opener, with round two at the Lausitzring on Sunday 6 May. Gary Paffett arrived as championship leader after winning at Hockenheim from sixth on the grid, with 25 points to Jamie Green's 18 and Mattias Ekström's 15. Ekström had taken pole there for Audi but finished third, and Audi's head of motorsport Wolfgang Ullrich had made it clear that the team needed to turn its qualifying speed into race results.

BMW came to Lusatia after a damaging opener. Andy Priaulx's sixth place had been its only top-ten finish, and Bruno Spengler had been eliminated on lap three after early collisions, so the new M3 DTM was still waiting to show what it could do over a full race.

chapters.title: Spengler takes BMW's first pole of the comeback
text: Qualifying was as tight as it had been a week earlier. Spengler's 1:18.777 in the top-four shoot-out put the BMW Team Schnitzer car on pole, 0.038 seconds ahead of his BMW team-mate Augusto Farfus, who had endured a difficult Hockenheim weekend. Paffett was third on 1:18.820, so 0.043 seconds covered the first three.

Mike Rockenfeller was the best Audi in fourth, having been quickest in Q1, and Edoardo Mortara missed the shoot-out by 0.062 seconds in fifth. Green was sixth, Martin Tomczyk seventh and Ekström eighth, after two small errors in Q3, so the first three rows held two cars from each manufacturer. Miguel Molina was ninth, and Adrien Tambay reached Q3 for the first time in tenth. Filipe Albuquerque missed Q3 by just 0.032 seconds and started 11th, while Timo Scheider, damaged after touching a kerb in Q3, lined up 12th, ahead of Andy Priaulx, Joey Hand and Robert Wickens in 13th to 15th.

Further back, Ralf Schumacher, Roberto Merhi and Christian Vietoris lined up 16th to 18th, with Susie Wolff 19th and David Coulthard 20th. Dirk Werner had a difficult session for BMW Team Schnitzer and started 21st, and Rahel Frey was last in the second Abt Audi.

chapters.title: Paffett on Spengler's gearbox
text: Paffett made the best start of the front runners. From third on the grid he went past Farfus before the first corner and was on the back of Spengler's BMW almost immediately, and the pair began to pull away from the field. Spengler soon had a cushion of around half a second, but it never grew much more than that. The Mercedes was quick in the corners, the BMW had the edge on the straights, and neither could create an opening on a track where passing is notoriously hard.

Behind them the grid sorted itself out. Green passed Mortara's Rosberg Audi for fourth early on, with Tomczyk close by, while Mortara, who had run fourth in the early laps, complained about a lack of grip and slipped back. Rockenfeller, who had started fourth, hit the kerbs hard at the first corner and dropped down the order, and Scheider moved from 12th to ninth on the opening lap.

chapters.title: Spengler stays ahead through both stops
text: With both mandatory stops still to come, Mercedes tried to use the pit lane to jump Spengler. Paffett was called in first and rejoined with a clean stop, but Spengler came in one lap later and also had a strong stop, which kept him ahead. The same thing happened at the second round, as Paffett stopped first and Spengler followed and emerged just in front again. Spengler's team had stretched the gap to around 1.5 seconds before both rounds, which proved just enough even though the Mercedes had the quicker stops.

The real strategy variation was further back. Green ran roughly ten laps longer than the other front runners in his first stint and closed on Farfus, but a slow final stop, when his mechanics struggled to fit a rear wheel, cost him more than three seconds, and he rejoined behind the BMW. Scheider ran a similar long first stint, moved up to sixth, and left the pits after his final stop alongside Ekström, who had gained a place from the start and passed Tomczyk after the first stops.

chapters.title: Spengler wins by 1.019 seconds
text: The last 16 laps were spent with Paffett right behind Spengler's rear wing, never more than 0.6 seconds back and never able to find a way past. Spengler took the flag after 52 laps in 1:09:45.795, 1.019 seconds ahead. It was his tenth DTM victory and the first for BMW since its return to the series.

Farfus was third, 7.069 seconds back, on only his second DTM start, and held off Green's Mercedes, who finished fourth 0.607 seconds behind him and set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:19.025 on lap 29. Ekström was a steady fifth, 21.362 seconds behind the winner, and Scheider sixth. Tomczyk took seventh for his first points of the season, Mortara was eighth and Albuquerque ninth. Ralf Schumacher gained six places from 16th on the grid to take the final point in tenth. Rockenfeller, who had started fourth, finished 13th after trouble at the first corner and a problem at his final stop, and Wickens was classified last after a late problem, having completed 47 of the 52 laps.

chapters.title: BMW celebrates, Paffett extends his lead
text: Spengler said he had to give 100 percent on every lap, with the Mercedes behind him attacking all the way, and that the team's strategy and pit stops had been decisive. He added that he had not imagined taking pole and his first win for BMW at only the second race. BMW Motorsport Director Jens Marquardt called it a historic weekend: it was the first win of the new DTM era for the marque, the 50th in the series, and he credited the pit crews, who had improved a great deal since Hockenheim. Farfus, on only his second DTM start, had shown he belonged on the podium, and Tomczyk and Hand showed good speed. Marquardt also warned that the series was so close that one result guaranteed nothing for the races to come.

For Mercedes it was a day of what-might-have-been. Paffett said his car had enough pace to win again and that the difference came at the pit stop, where he was a little too far behind, while running so close to Spengler had cost him downforce. Mercedes chief Norbert Haug said it was not enough to be faster at this track, where overtaking was so hard, and congratulated BMW. Green said he could not find a way past Farfus despite a strong car. Coulthard's 12th and Vietoris's 11th, after starting 20th and 18th, were not enough for points, and Schumacher's recovery from 16th to tenth earned the final point.

For Audi the afternoon was less satisfying. Ekström said the car lacked the pace to win, and Ullrich admitted that the team had again failed to get the tyres working properly in the race, while congratulating BMW on being competitive from the outset. The reigning champion marque had no one on the podium, and Rockenfeller and Molina, in 13th and 15th, left without points.

In the championship Paffett stretched his lead to 13 points on 43, ahead of Green on 30. Ekström and Spengler were level on 25, Farfus had moved up to fifth on 15, and Vietoris stayed sixth on 12. Spengler had gone from no points at Hockenheim to joint third. The DTM now travelled to Brands Hatch for round three on Sunday 20 May, the home race for both Paffett and Green.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler started from pole and won by 1.019 seconds from Gary Paffett, resisting pressure for most of the 52 laps.
